prompt: Write an email to a colleague about missing someone who is far away. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: Thinking of Maya (and a small favor)

Hi Dana,

I hope your week is going well. I wanted to write to you about something a little off-topic from our project, because I think you'll understand it better than most.

As you know, Maya moved to the Singapore office three months ago. I was genuinely happy for her. It's a great opportunity, and she deserves it. What I didn't anticipate was how much I'd miss her. It isn't just the work. It's the small things: the quick chats by the coffee machine, the way she'd lean over and say "okay, but what if we tried it this way?", the shared jokes that only make sense to the two of us. The team feels quieter without her.

The time difference makes it harder than I expected. By the time I'm settling into my morning, she's finishing her day. When I have a question, I find myself composing the message and then realizing she's asleep or offline. We've tried scheduling a weekly call, and I'm grateful for it, but it's not the same as a spontaneous conversation. A scheduled call has an agenda. Friendship, and good collaboration too, tends to happen in the unscheduled moments.

I've been trying to cope in practical ways. I send her short voice notes instead of long emails, since they feel more personal. We've started a shared document of articles and ideas we'd normally have discussed in passing. And I've made a point of telling her about the small, silly things that happen here, so she still feels part of the day-to-day. It helps, though it doesn't fully close the gap.

I'm telling you this partly because I suspect you've felt something similar. You mentioned once that you had a close friend working overseas, and I wondered how you handled it. Did you find anything that made the distance easier? I'd love to hear what worked for you, or even just that it gets less strange with time.

I'm also wondering whether we could do something small as a team to include her more. Maybe we could rotate who calls her during the week, or loop her into our Friday wrap-up by video. It wouldn't take much, and I think it would mean a lot to her, and to the rest of us.

No rush on any of this. If you have a few minutes for coffee next week, I'd enjoy talking it through in person.

Thanks for listening,
[name]
